title: Add audit receipts for all memory operations (v1.12.1)
context: Memory operations (grounding injections, agent briefings) left no trace of whether information actually reached agents, how often, or which records were never used. This opacity made debugging agent behavior difficult and compaction decisions guesswork.
decision: Implement a local ledger that records every memory operation. `hunch served` reads back the ledger to show what reached each agent, delivery frequency, and in-force records never consumed—turning invisible operations into auditable facts.
consequences: Full auditability of memory operations enables root-cause analysis of agent briefing failures
Identifies unused/ineffective memory records as compaction targets (records never-delivered are now visible)
Helper agents receive job-shaped briefings instead of generic ones (explorers get component map, planners get decisions + rejections)
Release gate no longer fails on its own memory commits mid-run; self-mutation no longer triggers false alarms
Two false-alarm classes eliminated: docs *describing* proposed status no longer grade as stale; backtick-quoted text is treated as example, not declaration
Warns when writes land in committed public store while private overlay exists—catches near-leaks before they happen
alternatives_rejected: No audit trail (original state—unmeasurable black box)
Centralized server-side audit log (chose local ledger for privacy and offline usability)
Generic briefings for all agent types (chose job-shaped briefings to reduce noise and irrelevance)
